diagnosis.summary: Flink checkpoint failures caused by a Chaos Mesh-induced taskmanager restart ~2 minutes ago; the job is already RUNNING/STABLE with 25 completed checkpoints in the last 5 min and is self-healing.
diagnosis.root_cause: A Chaos Mesh experiment (deployed ~144 min ago, with follow-up runs at ~31 and ~27 min ago) caused multiple pods to exit with code 255/Unknown. The Flink taskmanager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 was replaced just ~1.9 minutes ago (FlinkDeployment event: 'TaskExecutor is shutting down'), forcing the job to restart from its last checkpoint. The ~2.1 failed checkpoints in the alert window are from that brief restart transition. The jobmanager (uptime 96 s) and taskmanager are both Running/Ready, and the job is producing ~25 successful checkpoints per 5-minute window with no backpressure.
diagnosis.impact: Approximately 2 checkpoints failed during the Flink job restart transition, meaning exactly-once guarantees were temporarily suspended. Consumer lag is 650 messages; at normal throughput this will clear within minutes. No data loss is expected as Flink resumed from the latest successful checkpoint. All Kafka brokers are healthy with 0 under-replicated partitions.

evidence.finding: Job RUNNING/STABLE, uptime 96 s, restarts_last_15m=1.018, failed_checkpoints_last_10m=2.104, completed_checkpoints_last_5m=24.995, backpressured_fraction=0.0, consumer_lag=650. Taskmanager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 is only 1.9 min old (0 restarts), jobmanager last terminated 140.9 min ago with exit_code=255.

Warning JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 min ago: 'org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException: The TaskExecutor is shutting down' — confirming a clean taskmanager shutdown triggered the job restart.

Taskmanager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 age=1.9 min, restarts=0 (newly created). Ingestion pods also had exit_code=255 terminations ~140 min ago, consistent with a cluster-wide disruption event.
All 3 brokers Running/Ready; under_replicated_partitions=0, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0, active_controllers=1. Strimzi Ready=True. Consumer lag for flink-events-to-iceberg=650.

chaos-mesh-local was deployed at 144.6 min ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f), 31.3 min ago, and 27 min ago — all timing windows correlate with the mass pod exits (exit_code=255/Unknown) across the Flink, Kafka, and ingestion pods.
All 4 nodes Ready, no pressure conditions, no cordons. Workers span zone-a, zone-b, zone-c. No node-level failure.

proposed_action.rationale: The Flink job is already RUNNING/STABLE with checkpoints completing successfully (~25/5 min). The failures were transient, caused by a Chaos Mesh-induced taskmanager restart. The job resumed from its latest checkpoint automatically, and consumer lag (650) is small enough to drain on its own. Restarting any pod would be more disruptive than the current self-recovery.

follow_ups: Confirm Chaos Mesh experiment intent with the team: the three chaos-mesh-local deployments at 144, 31, and 27 min ago correlate exactly with the pod kill wave (exit_code=255). Verify these were planned experiments and not accidental or malicious runs.
Monitor consumer lag (currently 650) over the next 15 min to ensure it drains fully now the job is stable.

Review why the taskmanager was replaced 1.9 minutes ago (a second chaos experiment or a delayed operator reschedule from the earlier disruption) — check chaos-mesh CRs for active PodKill or PodChaos experiments.
Ensure the alert clears within the next 10-minute window as failed checkpoint rate decays to zero.
Note: the iceberg-exporter readiness probe was failing 27 min ago (2 events) — verify it is now fully healthy and iceberg table metrics are current.
